generation_method: Manually assessed against executable evidence gathered during AFENDA Phase 2 (control plane), Phase 2.1 (control plane hardening) and Phase 2.2 (toolchain authority/CI-evidence reconciliation). Unlike doctrine-registry.json / stack-registry.json / position-registry.json / authority-index.json, this file is not a pure deterministic text-extraction projection: implementation state is a judgment call that requires running real checks, not parsing prose. Structural completeness (every SCC-01..27 and V01..18 present exactly once, states drawn from the fixed enum) is itself verified by scripts/gate.ts's control-map-completeness step.
policy: A control is never 'implemented' merely because a document describes it; implementation requires an executable check.
A critical executable control requires at least one red fixture proving the gate actually fails on a real injected violation.
Absence of application/database/frontend code is represented honestly as not-yet-built, not as a passing or skipped control.
'partial' means a real, currently-passing executable check exists but does not yet cover the full required scope; the gap is named in notes.

eslint.config.mjs (type-aware lint via typescript-eslint), 0 errors

Phase 2.1: all 8 governance scripts (previously .mjs) rewritten as .ts with real types (no any, no unchecked casts, no @ts-ignore/@ts-nocheck) and confirmed to run directly under Node 24.18.0 with zero build step and zero emitted artifacts
red_fixtures: red:typecheck-native-injected-type-error (scripts/red.ts) — writes a disposable .ts file with a genuine type defect into the real tsconfig.json include scope and invokes the actual `pnpm run typecheck:native` command, confirming it exits non-zero, then removes the fixture
stack_controls.notes: Phase 2.1 closed both gaps recorded at the end of Phase 2. (1) The Phase 1 authority scripts (build-authority-registry, check-authority-integrity, lib/authority-parser) were migrated from .mjs to .ts with full types and are now included in tsconfig.json's strict scope alongside the Phase 2 scripts — there is no more excluded governance source and no ~180-error debt; both typecheck:native and typecheck:compat report 0 errors across all 8 files. (2) Two new red fixtures inject a real type error into the live tsconfig scope and invoke the production typecheck:native/typecheck:compat commands directly (not a helper-function mock), proving both compiler lanes actually turn red on a genuine defect. Implemented for the full scope that currently exists (governance tooling); there is still no application code, so this control's application-layer proof remains deferred to when packages/apps exist (see SCC-24).
stack_controls.revisit_trigger: When application packages exist, extend the same red-fixture pattern (real command, real injected defect) to the application typecheck scope.

red:lockfile-package-disagreement (scripts/red.ts, Phase 2.2) — mutates the real package.json devDependencies.turbo to a value that disagrees with the frozen pnpm-lock.yaml, invokes the actual `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` command (not a helper function), confirms ERR_PNPM_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE, then restores package.json byte-for-byte in a finally block
stack_controls.notes: Remains partial after Phase 2.2 investigation (this is a corrected, more precisely evidenced partial, not a re-opened question). Two things were investigated to completion and neither closes the gap, by design: (1) CI-observed evidence: `git remote -v` was run and confirmed this repository has zero configured remotes in this environment; there is therefore no GitHub Actions run that could possibly be inspected from here, and none is claimed. 'CI-verified' in SCC-04's wording remains unestablished, honestly, pending a real remote + an actual observed run. (2) The TypeScript-6 compatibility engine gap was fully traced (pnpm why/list, pnpm-lock.yaml snapshot line, node_modules/.pnpm inspection, the wrapper's own bin->lib->require chain) and independently reproduced from a from-scratch disposable install containing only the exact declared package specifier with no other dependencies present — ruling out local lockfile contamination. Classification: this is upstream package design (the @typescript/typescript6@6.0.2 wrapper's own package.json declares its real compiler engine, "@typescript/old", via the semver range "npm:typescript@^6", not an exact version) combined with a latent schema gap that stack/VERSION_BASELINE.json's schema_version 1 had — it had no field distinguishing 'package pin' from 'compiler engine' for this one tool. Phase 2.2 added that field (compiler.typescript_compat.compiler_engine) so the fact is now explicit machine authority rather than only checker-output prose. This is evidence/schema remediation, not a normative STACK.md contradiction: STACK.md's SEL-02 says 'exact versions' without specifying package-vs-engine granularity, and the frozen pnpm-lock.yaml does make the engine version deterministic and reproducible for this repository's tree (just not equal to the package-level reference_patch when the two are compared as if they were one fact). No STACK_AMENDMENT_PROPOSAL.md was created because the gap is fully resolvable through implementation metadata (done: VERSION_BASELINE.json + verify-toolchain-baseline.ts + red fixtures) without touching STACK.md's normative text. Separately, and now evidence-complete rather than gapped: stack/VERSION_BASELINE.json previously did not pin an exact pnpm or Turborepo version anywhere; Phase 2.2 added packages.pnpm and packages.turborepo entries recording the already-mechanically-enforced values (11.20.0, 2.10.8) as an explicit declared reference, closing that specific incompleteness. This did not require a STACK.md amendment either: SEL-04's binding constraints ('exact packageManager field, frozen lockfile') were already satisfied by package.json + pnpm-lock.yaml before this entry existed; VERSION_BASELINE.json is an unsealed machine-authority convenience registry, not sealed normative text. Also still true: turbo.json is schema-valid but currently orchestrates 0 tasks because pnpm-workspace.yaml matches 0 packages; `pnpm gate` invokes the underlying scripts directly rather than through `turbo run`.
stack_controls.revisit_trigger: When .github/workflows/gate.yml is observed executing successfully on a live GitHub Actions runner (requires a configured git remote first), AND either (a) the TypeScript-6 compatibility engine resolution is pinned exactly (e.g. a pnpm override/resolution forcing @typescript/old to the declared reference_patch) or (b) VERSION_BASELINE.json's typescript_compat.reference_patch is explicitly revised to match the intentionally-resolved engine version, whichever reflects the real governance decision.

evidence: scripts/build-authority-registry.ts regenerates governance/*.json byte-identically from doctrine/DOCTRINE.md, stack/STACK.md, position/POSITION.md (DET-01/DET-02 satisfied for the governance-registry layer: deterministic compilation from committed definitions, not an AI authoring claim). Phase 2.1 note: the only byte-level change from the .mjs->.ts migration in any of the 4 generated registries is the disclosed "generated_by" provenance string (now points at the .ts filename); every extracted object, hash, and count is unchanged — verified with `git diff` immediately after migration.

Phase 2.1: the toolchain-lock layer's own exactness was investigated more deeply (see SCC-04) and found to have a real gap (TypeScript-6 compatibility engine resolves via a transitive semver range to a patch different from the declared baseline) — this is additional, more precise evidence about the boundary of what is and is not yet provenance-proven, not a new capability

Phase 2.2: the toolchain-lock layer's reproducibility was independently verified, not just inspected — the TypeScript-6 engine resolution was reproduced from a from-scratch disposable install of only the exact declared package specifier, ruling out this-repository-local lockfile contamination as the cause. stack/VERSION_BASELINE.json was also completed with previously-absent pnpm/Turborepo reference patches, so the toolchain-lock layer's own DECLARED-vs-ACTUAL provenance surface (still governance-registry/toolchain-lock scope, not extended into the application layer) is now more completely covered than at end of Phase 2.1

doctrine_verification_controls.notes: Proven only for the governance-registry generation layer (doctrine/stack/position -> governance/*.json) and the toolchain pin layer. NOT proven for the application/financial system: there is no migration, ledger, or generator determinism to test yet, and GOV-05's 'complete verification bundle' is not yet fully assembled (no CI execution observed from this environment — confirmed in Phase 2.2 that no git remote is even configured here, not just that a run wasn't checked — no application dependency graph, and the toolchain lock itself still has the SCC-04 compat-engine gap, now more precisely documented). Marking this V-control implemented for the whole doctrine would overstate reality; 'partial' remains the honest state. Phase 2.2 did not expand this control's scope beyond governance-registry/toolchain-lock provenance — no application-layer generator or codegen determinism claim was added.
doctrine_verification_controls.revisit_trigger: When application-layer generators (codegen, migrations) exist and can be shown to regenerate byte-identically with a red fixture for hidden toolchain change at that layer too, and when the SCC-04 compat-engine gap is closed.
